sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: A mini savory snacks ordering app for a single shop: customers order on the website and the owner manages everything from a dashboard.

blocks.text: **Sabor de Mãe** is a delivery application for a single shop (no multi-tenancy) that sells mini savory snacks. Customers build an order by choosing a **quantity** (in steps of 10) and, optionally, the **flavors**; pick **delivery** or **pickup**; and pay with cash, card (in person) or **Pix** (they copy the key and send the receipt by WhatsApp). The owner receives orders in a dashboard, updates each order status and configures prices, opening hours, Pix and the brand look.

Small food businesses usually take orders by chat, repeating prices and rules by hand. Here the price is **always computed on the server**, opening hours are enforced automatically and customers follow their order with a code, with no account needed.

items: **End customer:** orders at `/pedido` and tracks at `/pedido/:codigo`.
**Shop owner (admin):** uses the dashboard at `/admin`.
**Developers:** API in `api/` and front end in `web/`.

items.title: Order without an account
items.text: Mixed or per-flavor quantity; lookup by an 8-character code.

items.title: Server-side pricing
items.text: Price table from 10 to 100 units, per-unit price above that and a delivery fee by tier.

items.title: Manual Pix
items.text: No bank integration: the customer copies the key and the owner approves the payment.

items.title: Opening rules
items.text: Daily hours, service days, manual “closed” switch and delivery turned off for a single day.

items.title: Owner dashboard
items.text: Orders, status, flavors, prices, Pix, opening rules and brand (logo and colors).

items.title: New-order alert
items.text: Sound in the dashboard (polls every 20 s) and optional push through ntfy.

blocks.text: The project is under active development (working MVP, deployed on Vercel with a Neon database). The original product brief is in `api/APP.md`.

sections.title: Quick start
sections.summary: From clone to a running app: API on `3333` and web on `5173`.

items: **Node.js 24** and npm.
A **PostgreSQL** database. The project uses [Neon](https://neon.tech) (the free plan is enough).
To run the API tests: a **second, separate database** (for example, a Neon branch).

blocks.title: Terminal
blocks.code:
git clone git@github.com:evelyndsl/sabordemae.git
cd sabordemae

blocks.title: api/
blocks.code:
cd api
npm install               # também gera o cliente do Prisma (postinstall)
cp .env.example .env      # PowerShell: Copy-Item .env.example .env
# edite o .env: DATABASE_URL, JWT_SECRET, ADMIN_USER e ADMIN_PASSWORD
npm run db:deploy         # aplica as migrations
npm run db:seed           # sabores, preços, configuração e usuário admin
npm run dev               # http://localhost:3333

blocks.title: web/
blocks.code:
cd web
npm install
npm run dev               # http://localhost:5173

blocks.title: Use port 5173
blocks.text: The API CORS only allows the `WEB_URL` origin (default `http://localhost:5173`). If Vite starts on another port, the browser blocks the calls: close the other process or adjust `WEB_URL`.

items: Customer: <http://localhost:5173/pedido>
Owner: <http://localhost:5173/admin/login> (user and password are `ADMIN_USER` and `ADMIN_PASSWORD` from the API `.env`)

blocks.title: First dashboard access
blocks.text: Open **Pix e contato** and register the WhatsApp number, Pix key, account holder and bank. Until the key is registered, the Pix option stays hidden from customers.

rows: `index.ts` exports the Vercel serverless handler; `server.ts` does the local `listen`.
Registers CORS, rate limit, JWT, Zod validation, the error handler and routes.
Defines endpoints and schemas. `admin/` applies the authentication hook to everything inside it.

blocks.title: Why two entry files?
blocks.text: Vercel requires the entry file to import `fastify` directly and export a function by default. That is why `src/index.ts` creates the instance and `buildApp.ts` (with no `export default`) holds the configuration. In development, `server.ts` starts the regular server.

items: `pages/order/` (customer) and `pages/admin/` (dashboard): one page per route.
`lib/api.ts`: **all** API access goes through here; stores the admin token in `localStorage` and handles 401.
`hooks/`: `useFetch` (with optional polling), `useSave`, `useStatusUpdate`, `useNewOrderAlerts`.
`lib/`: rules that mirror the API just to warn the customer before submitting (price, Pix deadline, opening rules).
`context/`: admin authentication (`auth.tsx`) and brand/theme (`brand.tsx`).

blocks.text: `FAIXA_PRECO`, `CONFIGURACAO` and `ADMIN_USER` have no direct relation to orders: prices and rules are read when the order is created and the result is stored on the order itself.

rows: `codigo` has 8 characters, is unique and is what the customer uses to look the order up.
Phone is digits only (mobile with area code, no 55). Not shown in the public lookup.
Delivery only. `numero` and `bairro` are null only on old orders.
Optional customer note, on any order type.
Copy of the shop address at order time (pickup).
Only orders with no scheduled time; set by the admin.
Pix only. Both null = pay at order time. The deadline is stored: changing the setting later does not alter old orders.

items: `ItemPedido.saborId` is **null** on a mixed order; `quantidade` is **null** when the customer only picked flavors (the shop splits the units).
Items are deleted with the order (`onDelete: Cascade`). Flavors are never deleted (`onDelete: Restrict`): they are deactivated with `ativo = false` because old orders reference them.

blocks.text: The `Configuracao` table always holds **one row** (`id = 1`) with everything the admin adjusts:

They live in `api/prisma/migrations/` (from `20261027182308_init` to `20261108120000_numero_e_bairro`). In production use `npm run db:deploy`; `npm run db:migrate` creates a **new** migration and is for development only.

blocks.title: Seed
blocks.text: `npm run db:seed` creates the 8 flavors, the 10 price tiers, the configuration and the admin. It **preserves** what the admin already edited; the admin password is always updated from `.env`. With `SEED_SOBRESCREVER=1` (used on the test database) base values go back to the defaults.

`PUT /marca` → `{ nome (2–60), cores }`. `cores: null` restores the default theme; each color is `#RRGGBB`, organised as `publico|admin` → `claro|escuro`.

`PUT /marca/logo` → `{ modo?: "claro"|"escuro", tipo: "image/png"|"image/svg+xml", dados: <base64> }`, up to 300 KB. The API checks the real content (PNG signature; SVG with no scripts, events or external elements).
`DELETE /marca/logo` removes the regular logo; with `?modo=escuro`, only the dark-mode one.
`GET /marca/logo?v=<version>` returns the image with long cache and headers that prevent active content from running; `404` if there is no logo.

sections.title: Business rules
sections.summary: The product rules in plain language, each with its source file.

blocks.text: The price is **always** computed on the server; any value sent by the client is ignored. The front end only shows a preview.

Both fees are editable (`PUT /taxa-entrega`); the 200 threshold is `entregaGratisAPartirDe`. Examples: 10 pickup = R$ 13.00 · 10 delivery = R$ 20.00 · 50 delivery = R$ 44.00 · 110 pickup = R$ 70.40 · 190 delivery = R$ 126.60 · 200 delivery = R$ 128.00.
Calculations use **integer cents** to avoid floating-point rounding errors.

items: **Mixed:** empty `sabores`. The response carries a single item `{ sabor: "Misto", quantidade }` and, in the database, a null `saborId`.
**With a quantity per flavor:** the sum must be exactly the order quantity.
**Flavors only, no quantity:** the shop splits the units; each item comes back with `quantidade: null`.
Mixing items with and without quantity, repeating a flavor, or using an unknown/deactivated flavor is rejected (400).
Source: `schemas/pedido.ts`, `services/pedidos.ts`.
Delivery requires `endereco` (5–300), `numero` (up to 20, “S/N” accepted) and `bairro` (up to 100). Blank text counts as not provided.
For pickup, `endereco`, `numero`, `bairro` and `pontoReferencia` are ignored and stored as `null`. The shop address (if configured) is copied to `enderecoRetirada`.
Old orders may have the number and district inside `endereco`.

blocks.title: Front-end note
blocks.text: Recent commits mention deliveries only in Paiçandu/PR and the removal of ZIP-code validation. That restriction appears as a notice in the front end (`components/aviso-entrega.tsx`); the API does **not** validate the city.

items: `horarioAgendado` is optional, must carry a time zone and be in the future.
No time = “whenever it is ready”: the admin sets the order prep time (`PUT /pedido/:codigo/tempo-preparo`) and the response carries `previsaoEm`.
An order with a scheduled time does not accept a prep time.
There is also a general minimum/maximum time (`GET /tempo-preparo`, default 30–60 min) shown to customers.

**Opening hours:** one daily `HH:MM` interval, the same every day. Both fields `null` = no restriction. Opening is inclusive and closing is not (at exactly 18:00 it is already closed). If closing is earlier than opening (18:00 to 02:00), service runs past midnight and the small hours belong to the day it started.
**Service days:** 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday. A day not on the list = closed all day. At least one day.
**Shop closed:** a manual switch that closes everything regardless of hours until turned off. **No** order is accepted, not even scheduled ones.
**Outside hours:** an order with no `horarioAgendado` is rejected; the customer may schedule it inside service hours. Every `horarioAgendado` must fall within service hours.

**Delivery today:** `entregaHoje: false` stores the day in `entregaSuspensaEm`, so the switch turns itself back on at midnight. Pickup only today: immediate delivery or delivery scheduled for today is rejected; delivery scheduled for another day is accepted.
The front end mirrors the rules (`web/src/lib/funcionamento.ts`) only to warn before submitting; the API always decides.
The app **does not confirm** payment nor integrate with any bank: the customer copies the key, pays and sends the receipt through the shop’s WhatsApp.
A Pix order only moves on after the admin checks the receipt and sets `PAGAMENTO_APROVADO`.
Initial key value: CPF `00000000000`, which is deliberately **not** a valid CPF: it is the “not configured” marker. With `configurada: false` the front end hides Pix.
Key validation by type: CPF and CNPJ by check digits; phone with area code; random must be a UUID. Phones get `+55` in `chaveParaCopiar`.

**When to pay** (`instrucaoPix`): order for today or with no time → right away (`imediato: true`). Order scheduled for a later day → at least a lead time before `horarioAgendado`: **2 h up to 100 units and 4 h above 100** (editable). If that limit has already passed, it becomes “pay now”. The deadline is stored on the order.

blocks.text: `precisaTroco` and `trocoPara` only apply to cash. With change, `trocoPara` is required and must be **greater than the order total**; otherwise 400.

items: Brazilian mobile numbers only: area code + 9 + 8 digits (`/^[1-9][1-9]9\d{8}$/`). Masks are accepted; a pasted `55` country code (13 digits) is stripped; only digits are stored.
The front end uses the same rule (`web/src/lib/format.ts`). It validates **format** only: there is no confirmation that the customer owns the number.
The phone never appears in `GET /pedido/:codigo`; only the admin sees it.

blocks.text: 8 characters from the alphabet `ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789` (no I, L, O, 0 or 1, to avoid confusion when read aloud). Generated with `crypto.randomInt`; on collision, up to 5 attempts.

PNG or SVG up to 300 KB, stored in the database itself. PNG is checked by signature; SVG is rejected if it has `<script>`, `<foreignObject>`, `iframe/embed/object`, `on...=` attributes, `javascript:` or `data:text/html`. The dark-mode logo is optional.

blocks.text: The API `.env` is in `.gitignore`. Only the `.env.example` files go in the repository.

Admin token secret, **at least 32 characters** (the API does not start without it).
The single origin allowed by CORS, no trailing slash. **In production, the front-end URL.**
`development`, `production` or `test`. In `test` logging and the ntfy alert are off.
Admin login created/updated by `npm run db:seed`.
A **separate** database used by `npm test`. Tests refuse to run if it equals `DATABASE_URL`.
ntfy topic for the new-order alert. It works like a password: use a long, random name. Empty = no alert.
Only if you host your own ntfy.

blocks.title: VITE_* variables are baked into the build

The shop WhatsApp, Pix key, account holder and bank are **not** variables: they are registered in the dashboard (**Pix e contato**) and stored in the database.

sections.summary: Every npm command, where it runs and when to use it.

rows: `tsx watch src/server.ts`: API with auto-reload at `http://localhost:3333`.
`prisma generate && tsc`: generates the Prisma client and compiles to `dist/`.
`prisma migrate deploy`: applies pending migrations. **This is the command for a fresh clone and for production.**
`prisma migrate dev`: creates a **new** migration from `schema.prisma` (development only).
Regenerates the Prisma client in `src/generated` (not in git).
Creates/updates flavors, prices, configuration and the admin.
`tsc -b && vite build`: checks types and builds `dist/` (same command as the deploy).
Serves the build locally for checking.
Vitest for the front-end rules; uses no network or database.
Checks that `pt-br.json` and `en-us.json` have the same structure.

sections.title: Testing
sections.summary: Vitest in the API (with a separate test database) and in the front end (pure rules).

blocks.title: bash
blocks.code:
cd api
npm test

items: They use the `DATABASE_TESTS_URL` database and **refuse to run** if it equals `DATABASE_URL` (`tests/test-env.ts`).
Before anything, `tests/global-setup.ts` runs `prisma migrate deploy` and the seed with `SEED_SOBRESCREVER=1`, leaving the database in its base state with a dedicated admin (`admin_teste`).
`tests/setup.ts` sets `NODE_ENV=test` and a test `JWT_SECRET` before the app is imported.
Routes are called in memory with `app.inject` (no port opened). Files run sequentially (`fileParallelism: false`) because they share the same database.

rows: Admin route protection, login, order listing and status, prep time, fees, prices, Pix and flavors.
Cash, card, Pix and invalid payment method.

blocks.title: bash
blocks.code:

npm test

blocks.text: They test the pure rules in `src/lib/` (price preview, Pix deadline, opening rules, formatting and masks, logo, theme and new-order detection), in `src/tests/*.test.ts`. They use no network or database (`environment: node`).

rows: `npm ci` → `npm run typecheck` → `npm test` (secret `DATABASE_TESTS_URL`; runs are serialised so they do not fight over the database).

items: Pure business rule (price, hours, deadline): test the function directly, with no database.
Route: use `app.inject` with `buildApp()` and the utilities in `tests/helpers.ts`; remember that data stays in the test database.
Never point tests at the production database.

blocks.text: `api/README.md` carries a complete manual test script for Postman (a `delivery-local` environment with `baseUrl`, `token` and `codigo`, scripts that store the token and order code, and more than 100 numbered scenarios).

sections.title: Project conventions
sections.summary: Conventions observed in the code and the git history.

items: TypeScript with ES modules (`"type": "module"`) in both projects; internal API imports use the `.js` suffix.
Domain names in **Portuguese** (`pedido`, `sabor`, `funcionamento`) and Portuguese comments explaining the *why*.
API: all input goes through a Zod schema; business errors are classes (`RegraDeNegocioError` → 400, `NaoEncontradoError` → 404, `ConflitoError` → 409) handled in `plugins/erros.ts`.
Money in integer cents in calculations; `Decimal(10,2)` in the database; 2-decimal strings in responses.
Front end: API access only through `lib/api.ts`; pure rules in `lib/` with tests; `@` alias for `src/`.
Front end: shadcn components in `components/ui/` (`base-nova` style); per-area CSS in `styles/components/`.
Front-end lint: Oxlint (`react/rules-of-hooks` as an error). No linter is configured in the API.

blocks.text: The history uses *Conventional Commits*-style prefixes, with an optional scope and messages in Portuguese:

blocks.title: Real examples
blocks.code:
feat: campos separados de endereço, número e bairro na entrega
fix(api): corrige o 500 na Vercel com um handler serverless
chore: Inclusão de templates para issues e PR
docs: remove referências ao WORKFLOW.md

blocks.text: Prefixes seen: `feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `docs` (and `bug`, used once). No `commitlint` or commit hooks are configured.

Observed pattern: `type/issue-number-description`, for example `update/1-update-adicionar-novos-campos-de-endereço`, `doc/inclusao-de-templates` and `update/4-adicionar-verificacao-de-telefone`. Changes reach `main` through a Pull Request.

flowchart LR
  I["Open an issue (template)"] --> B["Create branch type/N-description"]
  B --> C["Code and test locally"]
  C --> P["Open a Pull Request (template)"]
  P --> CI{"CI green?"}

items: **Issue** (`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issues.md`): title `[Feature] ...`, description, a “what must be done” checklist and notes.
**Pull Request** (`.github/pull_request_template.md`): what changed and why, `Ticket:`, “what was done”, “how to test” and “screenshots and notes”.
`cd api && npm run typecheck && npm test`
`cd web && npm run build && npm test` (and `npm run lint`)
Changed `schema.prisma`? Create the migration with `npm run db:migrate` and include it in the PR.
Changed a business rule? Update `api/APP.md`, the matching `README` and this documentation (`doc/content/*.json`, both languages, then `npm run check`).
No secrets in code or screenshots.

sections.title: Deploy
sections.summary: Two Vercel projects (API and web) and one Neon database.

items: Create a Vercel project pointing to the repository with **Root Directory = `api`**. There is no `vercel.json`: Vercel uses `src/index.ts`, which exports the handler.
Set `DATABASE_URL` (`-pooler` string), `JWT_SECRET` and `WEB_URL` (production front-end URL). Optional: `NTFY_TOPIC`.
Apply migrations and seed to the production database — Vercel does **not** do this:

blocks.title: bash
blocks.code:
DATABASE_URL="<string direta do Neon>" npm run db:deploy
DATABASE_URL="<string direta do Neon>" ADMIN_USER="<usuario>" ADMIN_PASSWORD="<senha forte>" npm run db:seed

blocks.title: PowerShell
blocks.code:
$env:DATABASE_URL="<string direta do Neon>"; npm run db:deploy
$env:ADMIN_USER="<usuario>"; $env:ADMIN_PASSWORD="<senha forte>"; npm run db:seed

items: Create a Vercel project with **Root Directory = `web`** (Vite is detected automatically).
Set `VITE_API_URL` to the production API URL, no trailing slash.
`web/vercel.json` rewrites any route to `/index.html`; without it, reloading `/pedido/CODE` or `/admin/dashboard` would give a 404.
Confirm that `WEB_URL` in the API is exactly this front-end URL.
**Migration before code:** always apply the migration **before** publishing code that depends on it.
**Approximate rate limit:** the limit (`/pedido`: 10/min, `/auth/login`: 5/min) lives in each instance’s memory; on serverless it is approximate.
**Single-origin CORS:** Vercel preview URLs (another domain) do not work with the production API.
**`trustProxy`:** on, so rate limiting uses the real IP from `x-forwarded-for` behind Vercel.

blocks.title: To be confirmed
blocks.text: To be confirmed: the repository does not document a rollback procedure. On Vercel a previous deployment can be promoted; Prisma migrations, however, have no automatic “down” and require a corrective new migration.

sections.title: Security
sections.summary: How the admin is protected and how personal data is handled.

items: A single kind of authenticated user: the **admin** (`AdminUser` table), created by the seed. Password hashed with **bcrypt** (cost 12).
`POST /auth/login` returns a 12 h **JWT**. Every route inside `routes/admin/` goes through an `onRequest` hook that verifies the token: no admin route is left public by mistake.
Unknown user and wrong password get the same answer and the same time cost (dummy hash) so users are not revealed.
In the front end the token lives in `localStorage` (`saborDeMae:token`); any `401` on an admin route logs out and returns to the login.

rows: A single origin (`WEB_URL`); methods `GET, HEAD, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS`.
All body/query/params go through Zod; price is always recomputed on the server.
Size, PNG signature and SVG with no active content; served with `nosniff` and a restrictive `Content-Security-Policy`.
500 errors return a generic message; details only go to the log.
`JWT_SECRET` with at least 32 characters, validated at startup; `.env` kept out of git.

items: Customers provide name, phone and (for delivery) address. This data is stored in the `Pedido` table.
`GET /pedido/:codigo` is public to anyone with the code, but it does **not** return the phone. Only the admin sees the contact.
The ntfy alert carries **no** personal data (only code, quantity, type and total) because the topic on the public server is open to anyone who knows its name.
The admin can permanently delete an order (`DELETE /pedido/:codigo`).

blocks.title: To be confirmed
blocks.text: To be confirmed: the repository has no privacy policy, order retention period or `SECURITY.md` with a channel for reporting vulnerabilities. Agree these with the project owner (likely relevant under Brazil’s LGPD).

blocks.title: Phone verification
blocks.text: Branch `update/4-adicionar-verificacao-de-telefone` validates the **format** of the mobile number. It does not send an SMS/WhatsApp code to confirm the number belongs to the customer.

sections.title: Troubleshooting
sections.summary: Common problems and how to fix them.

rows: API will not start: “Variáveis de ambiente inválidas”
`JWT_SECRET` shorter than 32 characters, empty `DATABASE_URL` or a `WEB_URL` that is not a URL.
Front end: “Não foi possível conectar ao servidor”
The API is not running or `VITE_API_URL` is wrong.
Start the API (`npm run dev`) and check `GET /health`.
The front end is on an origin different from `WEB_URL` (port other than 5173, a Vercel preview URL, a trailing slash).
Use port 5173 or set `WEB_URL` to the exact front-end origin.
The Prisma client was not generated (the folder is in `.gitignore`).
The seed did not run or the password changed in `.env` without re-running the seed.
Run `npm run db:seed` (it always updates the admin password).
Create a separate test database/branch and set the variable.
The Pix option does not show up for customers
The key is still the `00000000000` marker (`configurada: false`).
In the dashboard, open **Pix e contato** and register the key.
The function failed to start (missing variables, migration not applied or wrong entry file).
Check the variables, apply `db:deploy` and read the function log. The entry must be `src/index.ts`.
Opening `/pedido/CODE` directly gives a 404 on Vercel
`VITE_*` variables are baked into the build.
No new-order sound in the dashboard
Browsers only unlock audio after an interaction, or the sound is switched off.
Click anywhere on the page and check the sound button.

sections.title: Architecture decisions
sections.summary: Why the project is the way it is (short records, inferred from the code and comments).

blocks.title: To be confirmed
blocks.text: The decisions below were inferred from code comments and git history; review the reasoning with whoever made them.
ADR 1 — Price always computed on the server

items: **Context:** the front end shows a preview, but a customer could tamper with the request.
**Decision:** the API ignores any value sent and recomputes subtotal, fee and total (in integer cents).
**Consequence:** the price rule exists in two places (API and `web/src/lib/preco.ts`); the API is the source of truth.

blocks.text: ADR 2 — Manual Pix, no bank integration

items: **Context:** a small shop with no payment gateway.
**Decision:** the customer copies the key and sends the receipt on WhatsApp; the admin approves (`PAGAMENTO_APROVADO`).
**Consequence:** no gateway cost and no webhooks, but confirmation is manual.

blocks.text: ADR 3 — API as a Vercel serverless function

items: **Context:** simple, cheap deploys; the history shows a 500 fixed with a serverless handler.
**Decision:** `src/index.ts` exports a handler that creates Fastify once per container; `server.ts` handles local use.
**Consequence:** in-memory rate limiting is approximate; migrations do not run on deploy; the Neon pooler is recommended.

blocks.text: ADR 4 — Configuration in a single database row

items: **Context:** there is a single shop and the owner edits prices, hours, Pix and brand from the dashboard.
**Decision:** a `Configuracao` table with `id = 1`, plus `FaixaPreco` for the price table.
**Consequence:** no multi-tenancy; changes need no redeploy. The seed preserves what the admin already edited.

blocks.text: ADR 5 — Logo stored in the database and uploaded as base64

items: **Context:** serverless has no persistent disk and an upload plugin adds complexity.
**Decision:** PNG/SVG up to 300 KB sent as base64 JSON and stored in `Bytes`, served at `/marca/logo?v=<version>` with immutable caching.
**Consequence:** content validated on the server; each new logo changes the URL and busts the cache.
**Context:** the brief asks for a simple delivery-app flow with no customer login.
**Decision:** customers track their order with an 8-character code.
**Consequence:** anyone with the code sees the order (without the phone); there is no per-customer history.

blocks.text: ADR 7 — ntfy alert without personal data

items: **Context:** the owner must learn about new orders even outside the dashboard.
**Decision:** optional push via ntfy with a 3 s timeout and never throwing; message only with code, quantity, type and total.
**Consequence:** the topic name works like a password.

sections.title: Glossary
sections.summary: Domain terms, kept in Portuguese as in the code.

rows: A purchase made by the customer: quantity, flavors, delivery/pickup, payment.
The 8-character order identifier used to follow its progress.
A kind of mini snack (e.g. coxinha, kibe). Can be activated or deactivated, never deleted.
An order with no flavors chosen; the shop decides.
Bring to the customer’s address / the customer collects on site.
Date and time requested by the customer. Absent = “whenever it is ready”.
Brazilian instant payment method. Here it is manual: the customer pays and sends the receipt.
Proof of payment, sent to the shop WhatsApp.
Money returned when the customer pays cash with a note larger than the total.
The admin’s manual switch that rejects all orders.
A switch that turns delivery off for the current day only.
The shop owner, who uses the `/admin` dashboard.
The managed PostgreSQL service used by the project.
